user_clarification.summary: MediaPipe-generated hand landmark labels may be acceptable as a backup training-label source if human/manual sources are insufficient, provided MediaPipe is not used in browser runtime.
user_clarification.runtime_boundary: MediaPipe/OpenPose/YOLO/pretrained landmark systems remain disallowed as browser/runtime dependencies, feature extractors, model weights, or product authority.
user_clarification.training_label_boundary: Generated labels are not equivalent to manual labels, but may be reviewed as explicitly approved offline weak supervision.

second_response_summary: The claim that no human-annotated public hand-landmark dataset exists is not supported.
CMU HandDB, InterHand2.6M H partitions, and FreiHAND are higher-ranked candidates than MediaPipe-generated labels.
MediaPipe-generated labels should be offline fallback or augmentation only, with provenance disclosed and no MediaPipe runtime dependency.
Validation should prefer held-out human/manual labels and should not validate solely against MediaPipe-labeled data.

source_ranking.reason: Official page separates manual train/test hand keypoint annotations from synthetic and multiview-bootstrapped partitions.
Official page separates H, M, and H+M partitions and provides keypoint/bbox/validity annotation schemas.
Large official dataset with 21 hand keypoints and research-only terms; human-in-loop/optimization provenance needs review.
Official docs state labels were generated using Google MediaPipe.

preferred_order: offline generated-label weak supervision after documented insufficiency
generated_label_fallback_conditions: Manual and human-in-loop sources have been reviewed first and documented as insufficient for the exact training need.
The user explicitly approves the source, license posture, partitions, import/storage envelope, and generated-label provenance.
The student model starts from random initialization.
No MediaPipe/OpenPose/YOLO/pretrained landmark system is used in browser runtime, active feature extraction, model weights, or product authority.
Validation uses held-out manual/human labels where available and does not rely solely on generated-label agreement.
Receipts and manifests label the supervision as generated or weak_supervision, not manual.
